uncertainties: Whether the missing spec file is the primary cause of the agent's failure to proceed, or whether the agent would have skipped the workflow steps anyway
needs_review: The agent offered to proceed with reasonable defaults and bd human flagging, but never actually did so — unclear if this reflects a skill gap or just excessive caution

eval_feedback.overall: The agent scored 0/5. It correctly inspected the spec file first and identified real open questions, but then stalled completely — no epic, no tasks, no beads commands, no needs:discussion label, no bd ready/bd blocked check. The missing file was a recoverable situation (the agent itself offered to proceed with defaults), yet it chose to wait for user input instead of demonstrating the expected workflow. A skilled run should have: (1) run bd ready/bd blocked as orientation, (2) created an epic with child tasks using bd create --body-file -, (3) assigned numeric priorities, and (4) created a blocked issue with needs:discussion for the open design questions rather than just listing them in prose.

suggestions.assertion: Marks unclear or under-specified work with needs:discussion label plus blocked status
suggestions.reason: The agent verbally identified the right open questions but stopped there. The expectation requires actually creating an issue with the label and status — prose enumeration does not satisfy it.

suggestions.assertion: Uses an epic plus child tasks plus an acceptance review task rather than a native gate issue
suggestions.reason: The agent explicitly offered to create the epic and tasks with reasonable defaults, so the barrier was not capability but choice. A stronger agent would have proceeded after the file-not-found rather than blocking on user confirmation.

suggestions.assertion: Mentions showing bd ready and bd blocked before execution begins
suggestions.reason: This is a simple orientation step that costs nothing and was entirely omitted — it should appear even in a partial or blocked run.
